title: The Desperate letter to the council
subtitle: 困难与应对 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 困难与应对（做人与做事·困难与应对）
meta: 主题语境：困难与应对（做人与做事·困难与应对）　|　核心词汇：desperate　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 desperate 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1957 the counsellor wrote of ① a desperate letter to the council in the journal, and everybody in the garden said at once that it was ② more desperate than the one named there the year before. Three evenings on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the counsellor, who never explained anything, had done it twice over and gone home; it was the desperate ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most desperate letter to the council anybody in the garden had ever seen, or so the journal for June 1951 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too desperate to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the listener who had come to help; the desperate ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the letter at the far bench, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a desperate plan for the winter, and said that no listener in his right mind would call it ⑥ as desperate as the plan for the winter they had once had in the old garden. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was desperate or not, and he said so.

By 1964 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the journal. What the line asked for was ⑦ something desperate, and nothing besides. The listener from the next garden called the whole plan ⑧ quite desperate; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the journal kept the names of the desperate ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1967, year after year, she wrote of another desperate letter to the council in the same journal, and the work, which took two evenings, seemed ⑨ more desperate than anybody had expected. ⑩ The most desperate plan for the winter in the whole garden, she said in 1969, was the one she could never quite name; the desperate ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 绝望（前置定语 a desperate letter to the council：1957 年谈心人在心记里记下的那件绝望的信）
B. adj. 绝望／孤注一掷（比较级 more desperate than：文中两处，一处比写给议会的信，一处比预想）
C. adj. 绝望／孤注一掷（最高级 the most desperate：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 绝望（表语 too desperate to do：母亲觉得它太绝望，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 孤注一掷（前置定语 a desperate plan for the winter：叔叔把整件事称作一桩孤注一掷的最后一搏）
F. adj. 孤注一掷（同级比较 as desperate as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩过冬的最后一搏相比）
G. adj. 孤注一掷（后置定语 something desperate：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 孤注一掷（受程度副词修饰 quite desperate：那位倾听者的评价）

items.q: a desperate letter to the council
the most desperate letter to the council anybody
a desperate plan for the winter
The most desperate plan for the winter in

answers.why: desperate 意为“绝望”，1957 年谈心人在心记里记下的是“一件绝望的信”，此处作前置定语 a desperate letter to the council。
desperate 意为“绝望”，此处用比较级 more desperate than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
desperate 意为“绝望”，心记上 六月 那行字说它是小园里最绝望的一件，故用最高级 the most desperate letter to the council。
desperate 意为“绝望”，母亲认为这件东西“太绝望了，谁也用不上”，too desperate to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
desperate 意为“孤注一掷”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩孤注一掷的最后一搏”，此处作前置定语 a desperate plan for the winter。
desperate 意为“孤注一掷”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩过冬的最后一搏一样孤注一掷”，同级比较用 as desperate as。
desperate 意为“孤注一掷”，心记上那半行字要的是“孤注一掷的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something desperate。
desperate 意为“孤注一掷”，邻小园来的那位倾听者认为这套计划“相当孤注一掷”，quite 修饰原级 desperate。
desperate 意为“孤注一掷”，1967 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要孤注一掷”，故用比较级 more desperate than。
desperate 意为“孤注一掷”，母亲 1969 年说的是“整个小园里最孤注一掷的那一桩”，故用最高级 the most desperate plan for the winter。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1957 年，谈心人在心记里记下了一件绝望的信。（a desperate letter to the council）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更绝望。（more desperate than …）
母亲觉得它太绝望，谁也用不上。（too desperate to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩孤注一掷的最后一搏。（a desperate plan for the winter）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩过冬的最后一搏一样孤注一掷。（as desperate as …）
到了 1964 年，心记上只剩半行字：要的是一件孤注一掷的东西。（something desperate）
answers: In 1957 the counsellor wrote of a desperate letter to the council in the journal.
Everybody said it was more desperate than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too desperate to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a desperate plan for the winter.
He said nobody would call it as desperate as the plan for the winter they had once had.
By 1964 the journal asked for nothing but something desperate.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 desperate 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1957 the counsellor wrote of a desperate letter to the council in the journal, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most desperate letter to the council in the garden, or so the journal says.
My mother thought it too desperate to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a desperate plan for the winter, and nobody argued with him.
The listener from the next garden called the plan quite desperate, and everybody laughed.
The desperate ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
